candidate.blueprint_locator: Management of Care — quality improvement, performance improvement, and evaluation of care
candidate.blueprint_topic: Management of Care — nursing-sensitive quality indicators
candidate.educational_objective: Identify nursing-sensitive quality indicators and their relationship to nursing care and quality improvement.

options.A: Physician-sensitive indicators that primarily measure medical decision-making
options.B: Nursing-sensitive indicators that reflect structures, processes, or outcomes affected by nursing care
options.C: Unstructured observations that are not used for quality measurement
options.D: Billing indicators used only for reimbursement

candidate.rationale: Nursing-sensitive indicators are measures used to link nursing care with patient or system outcomes. ANA literature defines nursing-sensitive indicators as measures reflecting the structure, process, and outcomes of nursing care; falls and pressure injuries are established examples. B is correct.
candidate.source_claim_supported: Nursing-sensitive indicators reflect nursing structures/processes/outcomes; falls and pressure injuries are examples used to assess nursing care quality and patient safety.
candidate.source_document_title: Building Linkages between Nursing Care and Improved Patient Outcomes; Nursing and Patient Safety
candidate.source_locator: ANA/OJIN definition of nursing-sensitive indicators as measures of nursing structure/process/outcomes; AHRQ PSNet Safety and Quality Rating Systems — falls and pressure ulcers as nursing-sensitive care markers
candidate.source_organization: American Nurses Association (ANA); Agency for Healthcare Research and Quality (AHRQ)
candidate.source_version_date: ANA/OJIN 2013 foundational definition; AHRQ PSNet current page accessed 2026-08-17
